video_title: Michigan Star Morez Johnson Jr.’s Emotional NBA Draft Journey

quotes.speaker: Morez Johnson Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Morez Johnson Jr. reflects on his time at Michigan
quotes.excerpt: It's a weird feeling because you know you're leaving for better. I had so much fun here.
quotes.quote: This is my last full day here. I'm not sad or anything, but it's a weird feeling because you know you're leaving for better. I had so much fun here this past year, made real relationships, the staff, the managers, some of the players that are still here. So I'm excited. I'm excited.

quotes.speaker: Coach Akeem
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Akeem discusses Morez Johnson Jr.'s background and playing style
quotes.excerpt: Morez doesn't play like he's from the south suburbs, south side. He plays like he's from the west side.

text_blocks.speaker: Coach Akeem
text_blocks.text: This story like, so Rez is from the south side, south suburbs, and I'm from the west side. The dirty west side, guys. But Rez doesn't play like he's from the south suburbs, south side. He plays like he's from the west side.

quotes.speaker: Morez Johnson Sr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Morez Johnson Sr. on his son's work ethic and NBA dream
quotes.excerpt: I always told him, you are never going to wake up being good. You got to work hard.
quotes.quote: He told me in sixth grade he wanted to go to the NBA. My dream for my kids is always be successful and be good at what you do. And since we knew he was getting taller, I'm like, you should give basketball 100% because you don't want to be 6'7, 6'8, 6'9 and people ask you why did you play basketball? That's like the worst feeling in the world. I always told him, you are never going to wake up being good. You got to work hard.

quotes.speaker: Morez Johnson Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Morez Johnson Jr. credits his father for his work ethic
quotes.excerpt: My work ethic, I think it came from watching my dad work.
quotes.quote: My work ethic, I think it came from watching my dad work. My dad fixes washing machines and stuff, and I used to go to work with him when I was younger. He'd be in people's basements, sometimes the pump would come up, he'd be in people's poop and piss on the floor. All type of nasty foods on the floor, he got to be down there fixing stuff. So I think that kind of started my work ethic of like, I got to make the best of basketball. I love playing basketball, so why not take it as far as I possibly can?

quotes.speaker: Tai Streets
quotes.summary_phrase: Tai Streets on coaching Morez Johnson Jr. and his own career
quotes.excerpt: I played with Tom Brady and Charles Woodson, the greats. I was telling the kids, I made Brady.
quotes.quote: My name is Tai Streets. I used to coach Morez Johnson in high school, senior year at Thornton High School, and my main street's AAU basketball team, my Nike sponsored team. I played at Michigan from 95 through 98. I played wide receiver. I played with Tom Brady and Charles Woodson, the greats. I was telling the kids, I made Brady. I won MVP my senior year, so with Tom Brady on the team, I was telling the kids like, I made Brady.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on team dynamics and the importance of every player
quotes.excerpt: Every game is going to be different. We have to all be about whatever this team needs.
quotes.quote: When you came and contributed, guys, we have a long way to go. But because of the pieces we have in this locker room, for us to play like that and still walk out of here with the win, that's a testament to how talented you are. Now, every game is going to be different. We'll probably have a different starting lineup every game. We have to all be about whatever this team needs at this moment to win this game, and then the next game is probably going to be your moment or someone else's.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on his first meeting with Morez Johnson Jr.
quotes.excerpt: We took our entire staff over, we sat down with his family and his former coaches.
quotes.quote: The first time we met Morez was in at his old high school in a classroom, and we sat down. We took our entire staff over, we sat down with his family and his former coaches, and presented our plan for Morez, and we clicked. It seemed like from the very first meeting.

quotes.speaker: Morez Johnson Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Morez Johnson Jr. on Dusty May's vision for his role
quotes.excerpt: Dusty explained to me like, yeah, it might sound crazy right now, you're going to play the three.
quotes.quote: Dusty explained to me like, yeah, it might sound crazy right now, you're going to play the three, you're going to play the four, you're going to play the five. When I duck in, my like, you're going to, everybody going to slide down, you know, switch one through five, and our front court going to be insane. We got the pieces to win the national championship. We got a point guard that put y'all on the right spots to lead y'all. He basically laid it out to me, told me he's going to win, told me like, we at least going to the final four, and the rest is history from there.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on Morez Johnson Jr.'s decision to leave Illinois
quotes.excerpt: He just felt like he needed a change. He just wanted to be a little more involved.
quotes.quote: I don't think there was any bad blood towards the program for Morez or even his teammates specifically. He just felt like he needed a change. He just wanted to be a little more involved in offense. So his even his reasons for leaving were fairly unique, but they weren't they weren't near as selfishly as as the I think the Illinois fan base portrayed it.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on Morez Johnson Jr.'s growth and potential
quotes.excerpt: I expect he's a much better basketball player now, but I don't think there's much difference.
quotes.quote: I expect he's a much better basketball player now, but I don't think there's much difference in Morez now than even a year ago. He's granite, he's a rock, and man, I'm I'm rooting hard for him.

quotes.speaker: Jake Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Jake Davis on Morez Johnson Jr.'s return to Illinois
quotes.excerpt: I think he's going to hear it. That's all I know. I think the fans are going to.
quotes.quote: I think he's going to hear it. That's all I know. I think the fans are going to let him know. But I mean, as they should, you know, he left, you know, I think it'll be good for him to return to what what could have been, what what he could have had, but no, I think it'll be good, it'll be fun.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on how the team rallied around Morez Johnson Jr.
quotes.excerpt: When there was a side story like Morez going back to Illinois, our guys rallied around that player.
quotes.quote: The one thing we discovered about our team throughout the season was when there was a side story like Morez going back to Illinois or when when Yax made the comments about UAB or a die playing against UCLA, our guys rallied around that particular player. And while we were obviously competing for Big Ten regular season championship, which is one of the most difficult things to do in sports when you factor in the road environments and everything that that goes with it. That game, Morez knew that his teammates had his back.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on Morez Johnson Jr.'s future in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: He's going to be a long-time NBA player. The moment he walks into a locker room or facility,
quotes.quote: He's going to be a long-time NBA player. The moment he walks into a locker room or facility, the intensity will be elevated every day. The the level of seriousness and and the mental approach will be elevated as well.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on the value Morez Johnson Jr. brings to teams
quotes.excerpt: He's the type of guy that that's a championship level player. He's going to add value and
quotes.quote: It's going to be a very lucky GM and a very lucky organization to have him because he's going to he's going to add value and make an impact, not just the the first game or first exhibition game or Summer League. He's he's the type of guy that that's a championship level player.

quotes.speaker: Masai Ujiri
quotes.summary_phrase: Masai Ujiri congratulates Morez Johnson Jr. on being drafted
quotes.excerpt: You're gonna come sign your life away, and you're all mine... all mine!

text_blocks.speaker: Masai Ujiri
text_blocks.text: We got Patrick, the owner, he's on screen over there. Congratulations, man, we got the whole room here. Everybody is right here.

text_blocks.speaker: Masai Ujiri
text_blocks.text: You're gonna come sign your life away, and you're all mine... all mine!

text_blocks.speaker: Morez Johnson Jr.
text_blocks.text: Man, thank you. Appreciate you guys taking a chance on the kid.
